verdict.rationale: Name.com documents a transfer-in flow that requires the EPP/auth code (create-transfer endpoint plus an external-transfers guide). It also supports status tracking through a domain.transfer.status_change webhook. Transfer cost appears only indirectly, through a TLD price list covering 'each supported order type', and nothing addresses what happens to remaining registration time. missing for 10: explicit transfer-in pricing disclosure, documentation of how remaining registration time is handled (e.g., added year/term carryover), independent or hands-on corroboration of the transfer flow.

support.subject: As a power user, transferring domains IN is documented and honest — EPP/auth-code flow, status tracking, what the transfer costs, and what happens to remaining registration time

citations.quote: Initiates a domain transfer into your name.com account from another registrar. You must provide the domain name and its valid transfer authorization code (EPP code).
Subscribe to **`domain.transfer.status_change`** webhook events to track progress automatically.
moving a domain **from another registrar into name.com** (transfer in)
including pricing for each supported order type
